ProgramName: Master of Arts in Non-Profit Management
Requirements:
Applicants to the program must meet the following criteria:

Completion of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited university.
A grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 from prior undergraduate and graduate coursework.
Proficiency in English (if a graduate of a university in which English is not the native language) provided by an adequate TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language) minimum score of 550 with section scores of 50 or higher.

Submit an application
Pay the $35 application fee
Request/submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities previously attended to the email or mailing address above (including community college work and prior graduate work).
Provide a professional/personal resume
Provide a personal statement of 1,000 words or less in response to this prompt: Describe your experiences in the nonprofit sector and explain how those experiences have prepared you to succeed in nonprofit management.
Provide the names and email contact information for two recommenders in the application. [5]

[5] The program will focus on strategic planning, development of entrepreneurial skills, program management, fundraising, revenue generation and grant writing, human resources, technology, social media and marketing, legal issues, program evaluation and assessment. [1]

Description: The Graduate Certificate in Plain Language is the first and only program of its kind in an institution of higher education in the nation and was developed in response to the Plain Writing Act of 2010 and the Executive Order 13263 in 2011 which mandated clear communication in plain writing from all federal government agencies. [2] Plain language is a set of guidelines used to simplify and clarify communications addressed to the general public. [2] The guidelines include the use of simpler vocabulary, shorter sentences, lists, active voice, and shorter paragraphs, to name a few. [2] Although developed in response to the mandate for federal government agencies, plain language is an approach that is effectively used in many other areas, fields, and sectors besides federal government including: State and local government offices, in addition to federal government; Medical and health communication; Web design and web writing; Public relations and marketing. [2] This 12-hour graduate certificate can be completed fully online and is designed to enhance students' writing, design, and organization skills which can increase employability and/or help students reach new heights in their careers. [2] Any professional working for an organization that distributes information to the general public can benefit from developing and implementing skills in using plain language. [2]

This includes graduating from a high school accredited by a regional accrediting agency or holding a GED. Automatic admission is granted to applicants who graduate in the top 50% of their high school class, have a combined SAT score of 980 or higher on the Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Math sections, or an ACT composite score of 18 or higher. Students with an unweighted high school GPA of 2.5 or higher are also considered for automatic admission. Description: Political Science is the study of government—the most important decision-making institution in any contemporary society—and of the social and economic institutions and practices that influence this decision-making process. On the one hand, it is a discipline that can trace its roots to the ancient Greek political community, the polis; but it is also a modern social science, which uses techniques such as content analysis, public opinion surveys, and statistical analysis to create and evaluate generalizations about how government and people behave. Political Science is a broad discipline which is typically divided into four sub-fields: American politics, comparative politics (the study of foreign governments), international relations, and political theory. As a liberal arts discipline, the Political Science department is dedicated to developing analytical skills and promoting critical thinking. Students are encouraged to reflect not simply on their career goals, but also on what type of persons they want to become, and on their rights and duties as citizens.

In addition to work in the four language skills (listening, speaking, reading, and writing), the program of study offers courses in Peninsular and Latin American literature and civilization and in Hispanic linguistics, as well as a variety of courses in Spanish for the professions (translation, interpretation, business). Requirements: To qualify for freshman admission, applicants must submit an application via ApplyTexas, provide an official high school transcript, and submit SAT/ACT scores. [4] However, the University of Houston-Downtown is test-optional for most freshman applicants, who can choose to apply without submitting scores. [9] For formal acceptance into the Marilyn Davies College of Business for the BBA program, a student must complete the General Education Core for the State of Texas (42 hours), complete MATH 1324 with a grade of 'C' or higher, and have an established UHD GPA of 2.25 or higher (or a 2.25 GPA from the most recent institution for transfer students). [13]
Description: The BBA in General Business is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of the functional areas of business. The degree is particularly suited for students who have a focused career path in an industry that requires a breadth of business knowledge. It is well-suited for students who have a significant number of business credit hours from another institution as well as for students who desire to pursue a double-major within the college. Learning is achieved through a combination of lectures, case studies, and the application of concepts and models. In addition to providing a wide exposure to the functional areas of business, the program also stresses the need for effective oral and written communication skills and the use of information technology.
Accredidation: The University of Houston-Downtown's business and accounting programs, both graduate and undergraduate, are accredited by AACSB International-The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Insurance and Risk Management
Requirements: General application requirements for freshman applicants include submitting an online application (ApplyTexas or UHD Direct Application), paying a non-refundable $50 application fee, and providing an official high school transcript. [3, 9] Transfer students with 15 or more college-level credit hours must submit an online application, pay the fee, and provide official transcripts from all colleges attended, and must have a minimum 2.0 cumulative GPA. [5, 7]
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration degree with a major in Insurance and Risk Management provides a comprehensive program of study in insurance and risk management. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for professional careers in the risk management and insurance industry. Such careers could include opportunities in corporate risk management, employee benefits management, insurance brokerage, underwriting, claims adjusting, and financial planning. The coursework in this major may help students in their preparation for national professional examinations such as those for the Chartered Property and Casualty Underwriter (CPCU), the Certified Financial Planner (CFP) and the Certified Insurance Counselor (CIC) designations.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in International Business
Requirements: For freshman admission, applications are reviewed individually using a holistic process which considers overall grades, strength of high school curriculum, high school rank and GPA, and preparation for the intended major. [2] Submitting supplemental materials, including a resume, is encouraged. [2]
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration in International Business provides students with a broad overview of international business principles. Students learn about the complexities of international trade, including regional trade agreements, supra-national organizations, and foreign exchange systems. The program also develops an understanding of the strategies used by multinational corporations and how to manage in a cross-cultural environment.
Accredidation: The UHD Davies College of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Management
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) in Management provides students with a broad-based education in management. The curriculum is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to assume entry-level managerial positions in business, government, and not-for-profit organizations. Students gain a solid foundation in the functional areas of business and then proceed to more advanced coursework in management. The management curriculum emphasizes the development of analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. The program also stresses the importance of effective communication and interpersonal skills.
Accredidation: The Marilyn Davies College of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International). [2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Management Information Systems
Requirements: To qualify as a Freshman applicant, the student must have completed at least the 6th semester (junior year) of high school, received a high school diploma, or hold a GED high school equivalency. [4] Each Freshman applicant must apply online with the ApplyTexas Application (www.applytexas.org) and submit an official high school transcript. [2] Students who have completed the general education core (42 hours), earned a minimum 2.25 cumulative GPA, including a “C” in MATH 1324-Mathematics for Business and Social Sciences and satisfied TSI obligation may be admitted to the Davies College of Business. [9]
Description: The UHD Bachelor of Business in Management Information Systems program is based on a national model curriculum developed by educators and computer professionals, endorsed by the Association for Computing Machinery and the Association for Information Systems, and adopted by leading universities across the nation. [8] The student can choose from a variety of electives, including: Programming languages; Enterprise systems; Web technology; Information security; Microcomputer applications; E-commerce. [8]
Accredidation: The BBA programs of the Marilyn Davies College of Business are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business- International. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Marketing
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) program, a student must have completed 60 semester credit hours (SCH), including all lower-division program requirements. Additionally, a student must have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.25 at UHD and have earned a grade of "C" or better in all foundation courses.
Fees: The Spring 2026 undergraduate tuition rate for Texas resident students is $245.75 per semester credit hour and for nonresident students the rate is $655.75 per semester credit hour. [41]
CostPerCredit: $245.75 per semester credit hour for Texas resident students and $655.75 per semester credit hour for nonresident students for Spring 2026. [41]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Supply Chain Management
Requirements: To be admitted to the Marilyn Davies College of Business for the Bachelor of Business Administration program, students must have completed the general education core (42 hours), earned a minimum 2.25 cumulative GPA, and satisfied their TSI (Texas Success Initiative) obligation. A grade of "C" or better is required in MATH 1324 - Mathematics for Business and Social Sciences. [23]
Fees: The Spring 2026 undergraduate tuition rate for Texas resident students is $245.75 per semester credit hour. [28]
Description: Supply chain management is keeping track of products from raw materials to the point when the finished goods reach the customer, including planning and forecasting; purchasing; product assembly; moving; and storage. A major in Supply Chain Management, combined with a minor in an area such as engineering technology, marketing or management, provides students with a sound understanding of supply chain management and strategy.
Accredidation: The UHD Davies College of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International), a distinction achieved by fewer than 5 percent of business programs worldwide. [6]
CostPerCredit: $245.75 per semester credit hour for Texas resident students. [28]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological and Physical Sciences
Requirements: The application steps include: Apply for Admissions via applytexas.org, Apply for Financial Aid, Fulfill Testing Requirements, Get Advised and Register, Pay for Classes, and Prepare for Class. [14]
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Biological and Physical Sciences provides both a broad-based curriculum in the liberal arts and a specific set of courses in the natural sciences designed to meet the personal and career goals and interests of the student. [4] This degree is especially appropriate for students interested in multidisciplinary areas such as environmental science, earth/geological science, forensic science, life science, medical technology, public health, science education, and any health-related program that requires a bachelor's degree for entry into a particular graduate program. [4] Students interested in careers in teaching can pursue the B.S. in Biological and Physical Sciences with Concentration in Teacher Certification. [4]

Requirements: Each Freshman applicant must apply online with the ApplyTexas Application (www.applytexas.org) and submit an official high school transcript. UHD is test-optional for freshman admissions consideration with few exceptions. On your admissions application, you can elect to apply with or without submitting official SAT or ACT scores. [5]
Concentration: ['Cell and Molecular Biology', 'Ecology', 'Environmental and Evolutionary Biology', 'Microbiology/Infectious Diseases', 'Pre-Health Professions']
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Biology program at the University of Houston-Downtown (UHD) provides a comprehensive education in the biological sciences. The curriculum is designed to offer a strong foundation in modern biology, encompassing a wide range of subjects from molecular and cellular biology to ecology and evolution. Students in this program gain hands-on experience through laboratory work and have opportunities for research, preparing them for diverse career paths. The program aims to develop students' analytical and problem-solving skills, enabling them to pursue advanced studies in graduate or professional schools (e.g., medical, dental, veterinary), or to enter careers in research, healthcare, biotechnology, education, and environmental science.

The Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology is an interdisciplinary program, with a curriculum that has a strong foundation in the basic sciences, as well as incorporates courses from the Departments of Computer Science and Engineering Technology, Criminal Justice and Social Work, and the College of Business. This degree provides students with a broad-based science and technology education that includes hands-on experience in our state-of-the-art laboratories and prepares them for employment in this rapidly expanding field. Biotechnology uses living organisms or their products for commercial purposes. The field has a broad range of applications from medicine and diagnostics to agriculture and the food industry, to forensics and bioremediation. Biotechnology is a major engine for the economic growth in the Houston area with the Texas Medical Center and the Johnson Space Center.

Requirements: Freshman applications are reviewed individually through a holistic review process. Factors considered include overall grades in academic coursework, trends in achievement, the strength and rigor of the high school curriculum (including AP, IB, and dual credit courses), high school rank, and GPA. [2] Applicants are encouraged to submit supplemental materials. [2]
Description: The B.Sc. in Chemistry program provides students with takeaways in the traditional branches of chemistry including analytical, organic, inorganic, physical and biochemistry. The program also emphasizes development of IT and communication skills. Students develop practical skills through laboratory courses utilizing state of the art equipment. An internship placement provides students with training and preparation for the workplace. All students obtain experience in research through a project completed in their final year. Graduates of the program are well prepared to take up positions in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries or pursue further studies at the graduate level.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Communication Studies
Requirements: The specific program page does not list admission requirements for the university, but for declaring the major. To declare a major in Communication Studies, a student must have completed 15 semester credit hours and have a University of Houston-Downtown GPA of 2.0 or higher. General freshman admission to the university requires a high school diploma or GED. [2] For applicants from high school, admission criteria are based on a combination of class rank and GPA or test scores. [8] For example, an applicant in the second quarter of their class (26-50%) must have a minimum SAT score of 930 or an ACT of 18, or a 2.5 GPA. [8]
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Concentration: ['Corporate Communication', 'Human Relations Communication', 'Political Communication', 'Strategic and Risk Communication', 'Global and Intercultural Communication']
Description: The Bachelor of Communication Studies degree prepares students to act as expert communicators in a variety of contexts. Students have the opportunity to pursue one of five different tracks based on their career goals, including corporate communication, human relations communication, political communication, strategic and risk communication, and global and intercultural communication. Elective courses give students the opportunity to declare a minor that fits their specific interests.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (BS CS) provides an in-depth foundation in programming, software development, technology systems, science, and math. You may find this degree of interest if you want to pursue software development as a career path or go to graduate school in computer science. There is a required Capstone Project for students seeking this degree.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice
Requirements: Declaration as a Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice (BSCJ) major requires that continuing students at UHD have a UHD GPA of 2.0 or higher. [14] Students transferring to UHD must have a transfer GPA of 2.0 or higher. [14] Freshmen who meet the Freshman Admissions criteria will be declared upon admission to the university. [14]
Description: Course work leading to a bachelor's degree equips students with a foundation in criminological theories and criminal justice processes, including analytical and critical thinking skills. The Criminal Justice faculty strive to prepare students to be effective leaders in criminal justice and related fields, as well as research and advanced studies. Graduates who earn a BS in Criminal Justice will be able to: Critically analyze crime and justice issues. Apply criminological and justice system theories to the study of crime and justice. Communicate effectively about criminal justice topics. Analyze criminal justice ethical dilemmas and develop sound courses of action. Apply research methods and statistical analyses to criminal justice problems. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Data Science
Requirements: Students wishing to major in Data Science must meet the university’s general admission requirements.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Data Science degree is designed to provide students with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills in data science. Through this program, students will learn the fundamentals of statistical and computational tools and methods appropriate for managing and processing Big Data. The curriculum is a mix of theoretical topics and project driven coursework. This interdisciplinary program brings together coursework from computer science, statistics, and mathematics. The degree requires a minimum of 120 credits. Credits will come from required coursework in math, computer science, and statistics. Students must also complete courses from a diverse list of approved technical electives. Students must also complete all university general education requirements.

Requirements: UHD freshman applicants have the option to apply for admission with or without SAT/ACT test scores. On the application, you will select whether you want your application to be reviewed with test scores or without test scores (test optional). Please note that if admitted without test scores, students will still need to fulfill the TSI requirement​ prior to enrollment into classes. [7]
Description: The Geosciences program provides education in fundamental principles and applications in geosciences through theoretical, laboratory, and field experience. Students gain a broad and versatile knowledge in geosciences, providing them with qualifications and skills suitable for employment in governmental and private sectors concerned with environmental evaluation, energy and mineral resources, and groundwater exploration. The program also prepares students to conduct research through higher degree studies. Students are engaged in research projects in their junior or senior year and participate in a range of departmental research activities. Students are offered introductory work experience in private companies and public utilities and agencies through an internship program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health and Behavioral Science
Requirements: To be admitted into the Bachelor of Science in Health and Behavioral Science program, students must meet the general freshman admission requirements for the University of Houston-Downtown. Applicants must submit an online application via ApplyTexas, pay a non-refundable application fee, and provide an official high school transcript. [2, 7] UHD is generally test-optional, meaning applicants can choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT scores, though some exceptions apply (e.g., GED and homeschool applicants are not eligible for test-optional admission and must submit scores). [7, 11]
Concentration: ['Aging and Wellness Concentration', 'Healthcare Navigation Concentration', 'Heath and Wellness Concentration']
Description: The Health and Behavioral Science degree combines a liberal arts education with traditional health curriculum, which prepares graduates for entry-level careers in health and/or geriatric care, two of the fastest growing industries in the United States. [2] Health and Behavioral Science majors select one of two career tracks: Healthcare Navigation or Aging & Wellness. [2] Students in the Healthcare Navigation track complete courses such as Medical Case Management and Patient Advocacy, while students in the Aging & Wellness track complete courses such as Wellness and Aging and Long-Term Care. [2] The Health and Behavioral Science degree is interdisciplinary, which allows students to gain an understanding of health and aging from a variety of academic perspectives including biology, public health, psychology, communication, and sociology. [2] As Health and Behavioral Science majors near graduation, they are able to gain employment experience or preparation for graduate school by participating in either an internship or faculty supervised research. [2] Graduates of the Health and Behavioral Science program will: Examine the biological, psychosocial, and political factors that influence health and/or gerontology, Communicate effectively within the healthcare and/or gerontological context, Utilize basic research methods and statistics to assess and interpret health and/or gerontological research, Function professionally in healthcare and/or gerontological settings, and Identify and analyze ethical dilemmas within the healthcare and/or gerontology fields to determine an appropriate course of action. [4]
Accredidation: The University of Houston-Downtown is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award baccalaureate and masters degrees. [7] There is no mention of a specific accreditation for the Bachelor of Science in Health and Behavioral Science program. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies
Requirements: The program-specific page does not list unique application requirements. It refers to the general university admission requirements for baccalaureate degrees. Applicants must satisfy the general admission requirements of the University of Houston-Downtown.
Description: An interdisciplinary major can broaden your academic knowledge and equip you with an array of skills relevant for entry into many occupations. Employers value critical-thinking, teamwork, and solid communication skills. They seek employees who can handle complex information and solve real-world problems. The Interdisciplinary Studies degree is customizable to meet your academic goals within the parameters of degree requirements and prerequisites. [5]

The BS in Mathematics is an 120-hour degree program that includes several concentrations that students can choose to meet their career goals. For students interested in a career using actuarial science, the Actuarial Science concentration prepares them for the first two exams that are required to become a certified actuary. For students interested in using mathematics to solve real-world problems in business, engineering or science, the Applied Mathematics concentration would be an excellent choice. For students interested in teaching mathematics at the secondary level (grades 7-12) the Secondary Education concentration provides the content background to do that. For students interested in a career in a data-rich field, the Statistics concentration would be appropriate. In addition to the concentrations above, students may also pursue a general BS in Mathematics without a concentration.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nursing (RN to BSN)
Requirements: Applicants to the RN to BSN track must have graduated from an accredited associate degree or diploma program. Applicants must provide evidence of an unencumbered, current Texas Registered Nurse license. Applicants must have completed all required nursing program requirement course work prior to enrolling in the program. Applicants must satisfy all university core requirements for an undergraduate degree in addition to the track requirements.
Description: The RN to BSN program is designed for the registered nurse who is a graduate of an associate degree or diploma program in nursing and is ready to expand their nursing education. The curriculum is designed to provide the registered nurse with a broad knowledge base in nursing, the humanities, and the social and physical sciences. The program provides the necessary background for promotion in the clinical setting and for entrance into a graduate program in nursing. All nursing courses are offered online. This degree consists of 34 semester credit hours of study in nursing, a 3 semester credit hour course in statistics, and completion of a 42 semester credit hour university core curriculum.
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Political Science
Requirements: To qualify as a Freshman applicant, the student must have completed at least the 6th semester (junior year) of high school, received a high school diploma, or hold a GED high school equivalency. [2] Each Freshman applicant must apply online with the Apply Texas Application (www.applytexas.org) and submit an official high school transcript, and SAT/ACT test score results. [2] An admission decision is not made until the applicant's file is complete. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Professional Writing
Requirements: The provided program URL focuses on the curriculum and learning outcomes for the Bachelor of Science in Professional Writing, not the initial application requirements to the university. General freshman admission to the University of Houston-Downtown is based on a holistic review process that considers overall grades, strength of high school curriculum, high school rank and GPA, and preparation for the intended major. [2] Applicants are encouraged to submit supplemental materials, which include a resume. [2]
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Professional Writing prepares students for careers that involve writing in business and industry, the sciences, and the government. Our program emphasizes three primary areas of professional and technical writing: technical, scientific, and business writing; creative, nonfiction writing, editing, and publishing; and new media and electronic writing. UHD’s location in a major metropolitan area provides students with numerous opportunities for internships in professional and technical communication. The program prepares students to enter a variety of fields including technical and scientific writing and editing, medical writing, software documentation, grant and proposal writing, and public relations.

Requirements: To complete a BS in Psychology, students must satisfy the “Requirements for CHSS Majors ” and fulfill the coursework listed on the program page. [5] The program is 120-credit-hours. [12] General freshman applicants are reviewed individually using a holistic review process considering overall grades, strength of high school curriculum, high school rank and GPA, and preparation for the intended major. [3]
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Concentration: The department also offers five optional concentrations that allow students to focus their studies in a particular area of psychology. These concentrations are: Clinical/Counseling Psychology, Industrial-Organizational Psychology, Neuroscience, Forensic Psychology, General Psychology.
Description: Psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. The Bachelor of Science in Psychology at UHD is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of this fascinating field, including the major theoretical perspectives, research methods, and practical applications. Students will explore the biological, cognitive, social, and emotional bases of human behavior, as well as the effects of culture and diversity. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, scientific reasoning, and effective communication skills. Students will learn to apply psychological principles to real-world problems and to evaluate psychological research and claims. The program also provides opportunities for students to gain hands-on experience through research and fieldwork.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Social Sciences
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Science degrees with majors in Social Sciences are interdisciplinary degrees meant to prepare the graduate with a general foundation across the social sciences, and the experience of deeper inquiry in at least two areas of study in the social sciences. For purposes of these degrees, the social sciences include history, political science, psychology and sociology. [5] Graduates who earn a BA/BS in Social Sciences will be able to: Apply specific social science theory to real world situations and recommend a best course of action; Demonstrate proficiency in empirical social science research; Effectively write generalizations, and weigh conflicting evidence in their writing. [6]
Accredidation: University of Houston-Downtown is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award baccalaureate and masters degrees. [8] No specific accreditation for the Bachelor of Science in Social Sciences program is mentioned on the provided page.
CostPerCredit: $245.75 per semester credit hour for Texas resident students and $655.75 per semester credit hour for nonresident students. [33]

Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission, new students must submit an application through the ApplyTexas Application (www.applytexas.org) and pay a non-refundable application fee. Freshman applicants must submit an official high school transcript. The university is test-optional for most freshman applicants, who can choose to apply with or without submitting official SAT or ACT scores. [2, 7] However, applicants such as GED and homeschool students are not eligible for the test-optional policy and must submit test scores. [2]
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Sociology is designed for students with career interests in applied social research in either the public or private sectors. This degree option provides students with more extensive training in research methodology and statistics than is available through the Bachelor of Arts degree. The BS in Sociology prepares students for entry-level positions in social research and for graduate study in sociology and other related fields.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Statistics provides a strong foundation in the statistical and mathematical sciences and is designed to prepare students for careers or graduate study in statistics and other fields involving the analysis and interpretation of data. Statistics is a science that involves the extraction and processing of information from data. Statisticians develop methods for collecting data and use those methods to analyze and interpret data in a variety of fields, including business, industry, government, and scientific research. The BS in Statistics curriculum provides students with a broad set of skills in data analysis, statistical modeling and computation and statistical theory.

Requirements: To declare a major in Social Work, a student must have earned 24 semester credit hours and have a minimum cumulative UHD GPA of 2.5. Students must also complete specific prerequisite courses, including ENG 1301, ENG 1302, MATH 1301, and POLS 2305, with a grade of 'C' or better. It is also recommended that students complete a statistics course. The program requires a total of 120 credit hours for the degree.
Description: The University of Houston-Downtown Social Work Program is a dynamic, student-centered, community-focused, and culturally diverse program that prepares undergraduate students for entry-level generalist social work practice. The Program is committed to the development and maintenance of a quality educational program that provides a curriculum based on the liberal arts and the knowledge, values and skills of the social work profession. The UHD Social Work Program curriculum is designed to ensure that students are provided a solid foundation for understanding and embracing the values and ethics of the social work profession, while focusing on social and economic justice. Our mission is to educate social workers to be effective, ethical, and committed professionals who are agents of change and advocates for social justice.
Accredidation: The University of Houston-Downtown Social Work Program is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education’s Board of Accreditation.

Requirements: Students seeking a minor in Accounting must satisfy the prerequisites for the minor and complete 18 credit hours of specified upper-level accounting coursework. To declare a minor, a student must have a 2.0 or higher UHD GPA and be in good academic standing. [9, 10]
Description: The Minor in Accounting is available to all non-accounting business majors and to non-business majors. The minor will allow students in these two groups to develop a sufficient understanding of accounting to benefit them in their major field of study and in their careers. It will also allow them to better understand and use accounting information. The minor requires a minimum of 18 semester credit hours (SCH) of accounting course work, of which at least nine must be at the upper-level. At least nine SCH for the minor, of which six must be upper-level, must be completed at UHD. A grade of C or better must be earned in all courses for the minor.

ProgramName: Minor in African and African-American Studies
Requirements: A student wishing to minor in African and African-American Studies must complete 18 semester credit hours, of which 9 must be from the upper-level (3000-4000) courses, with a grade of "C" or better in each course. The 18 hours must be distributed as follows: AMST 2301 or AMST 2302 and 15 semester credit hours of interdisciplinary electives chosen in consultation with the Director of the program in African and African-American Studies.
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The minor in African and African-American Studies is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the experience of people of African descent. The minor is designed to provide students with a broad liberal arts education, focusing on a variety of subjects, including history, humanities, and the social sciences. Students are required to take 18 semester credit hours of study, 12 of which must be in upper-level courses. All students who minor in African and African-American Studies must take AAAS 2301. The remaining 15 hours should be selected from the list of approved courses below.

Requirements: To declare a minor in Applied Statistics, a student must have a GPA of 2.0 or greater and have successfully completed MATH 1305, MATH 1306, and STAT 3309 or MATH 2401, MATH 2402, and MATH 3302.
Description: The minor in Applied Statistics is intended to provide students with a solid foundation in the concepts of statistical data analysis. The minor will require 18 credit hours of course work in mathematics and statistics. The courses in the minor will provide students with the necessary knowledge to implement a variety of the more common statistical methods. Knowledge of these methods and the experience of using a modern statistical software package, will allow students to effectively analyze real data. The minor is a valuable asset to students who are majoring in a variety of fields including business, social sciences, natural sciences, and education. Students planning to enter a graduate program that requires a research component will find that the knowledge gained in the minor will be very helpful. All courses in the minor must be completed with a grade of C or better.

Requirements:
A student may minor in Art by completing 18 semester credit hours as follows. A grade of “C” or better must be earned in all minor courses.

ART 1301 - History of Art I (3)
ART 1302 - History of Art II (3)
6 hours from 2000-level ART courses

Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The minor in Art requires 18 semester credit hours of art courses, at least 6 of which must be upper-level. Students must earn a grade of "C" or better in all courses for the minor.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $4,000 per year for the TEACH Grant. [12] Merit scholarships up to $2,000 per year are also available for freshmen. [11]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, need-based, and departmental scholarships are available. [11, 12, 15]

Requirements: 22 hours of biology with only eight hours at the lower level: must include a minimum of four three-contact hour laboratory courses. Minors require a minimum GPA of 2.0 in all applied coursework. Upper level courses applied to a minor must have a grade of C or better. Minors must be distinct from any declared degree and degree concentration. Students may bring 3-4 hours of upper-level credit from another institution, but the balance of upper-level credits (depending upon minor) must be taken at UHD. Credit for directed studies, field experiences, honors thesis and undergraduate research cannot apply. [20]
Description: To earn a minor in biology, a student must complete 18 semester credit hours of biology courses, of which at least 12 must be at the upper-level. A grade of “C” or better must be earned in all courses for the minor. Students with majors in the College of Sciences and Technology must have a minor outside their major field of study. For the Bachelor of Science in Biological and Physical Sciences, the minor must be in an area other than biology or chemistry. For the Bachelor of Science in Biology, the minor cannot be in biology.

Requirements: Minors require a minimum GPA of 2.0 in all applied coursework. Upper level courses applied to a minor must have a grade of C or better. Minors must be distinct from any declared degree and degree concentration. Students may bring 3-4 hours of upper-level credit from another institution, but the balance of upper-level credits must be taken at UHD. Credit for directed studies, field experiences, honors thesis and undergraduate research cannot apply. The minor requires 21 hours of Chemistry, which must include CHEM 1307, CHEM 1107, CHEM 1308, CHEM 1108, CHEM 3301, CHEM 3201, and eight hours of upper-level chemistry. [9]
Description: The minor in chemistry requires a minimum of 19 semester credit hours in chemistry. A grade of “C” or better is required in all courses for the minor. The minor is available to any non-chemistry major.

Requirements: To declare a minor, a student must have a major and be in good academic standing. The Minor in Communication consists of 18 semester credit hours, of which 9 must be at the 3000-level or higher. A grade of 'C' or better is required in all courses for the minor.

To declare a minor in computer science, a student must have a 2.5 GPA in all courses that count toward the major and a 2.5 GPA in all courses taken at UHD. The computer science minor consists of a minimum of 18 semester credit hours of computer science courses, including 9 advanced.

The minor in Creative Writing requires the successful completion of 18 semester credit hours (SCH), 9 of which must be advanced (3000- or 4000-level), and 9 of which must be in residence at UHD. The requirements include 3 semester credit hours of ENG 2307 - Introduction to Creative Writing, 9 semester credit hours from a selection of creative writing courses, and 6 semester credit hours of electives from other specified English courses.
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The University of Houston-Downtown (UHD) has an exciting Creative Writing Program with robust course offerings taught by engaged and well-published faculty. [4] Our program fosters a community of aspiring writers, poets, literary translators, and editors. [4] Students explore their imagination and critical thinking, while studying different genres and reading authors from diverse backgrounds and literary traditions. [4] Students at University of Houston-Downtown can be part of the Creative Writing Program in two ways: 1) They can pursue a BA in English with a concentration in Creative Writing or 2) minor in Creative Writing. [4]

Requirements: A student must complete all course work required for the minor in addition to all course work required for the degree prior to graduation certification.
